title: Processes, deploy modes and ports
outcome: Trace driver and executor placement and distinguish browser ports from Spark RPC.

title: Prepare and identify compatible images
outcome: Bind a native prepared Spark image to its immutable identity and explain notebook preparation.

title: Own an isolated Compose topology
outcome: Start and resume a scoped master/two-worker/separate-driver lab without registry access or state deletion.

title: Submit a bounded distributed fit
outcome: Check partition coverage, closed-form fitting and future-covariate prediction without collecting observations.

title: Run supported Standalone cluster jobs
outcome: Distinguish supported JVM cluster submission from unsupported Standalone Python cluster mode.

title: Use Jupyter as a client-mode driver
outcome: Connect an explicitly prepared notebook kernel to executors and clean up its owned Spark session.

title: Repair driver DNS and callback routes
outcome: Diagnose a reachable master with an unreachable advertised driver address.

title: Distribute Python, JVM and native dependencies
outcome: Place each dependency at its actual importing process and test source/architecture identity.

title: Inspect a live Spark UI securely
outcome: Bind UI evidence to the actual application while keeping access scoped to loopback or an authorized tunnel.

title: Retain event logs and read completed history
outcome: Inspect completed application history after container replacement without replaying its computation.

title: Separate scratch, checkpoints and published state
outcome: Identify which state must survive worker, driver and container failure and choose a compatible storage boundary.

title: Budget memory, cores, PIDs and results
outcome: Diagnose memory, thread and result-size failures using distinct resource evidence.

title: Observe controlled worker loss and recovery
outcome: Bind an owned in-flight worker stop to task attempts and complete numerical result coverage.

title: Submit Kubernetes cluster-mode applications
outcome: Review an explicit-target Kubernetes submission and distinguish allocation, image and application failures.

title: Connect Kubernetes notebook drivers
outcome: Give one notebook driver a reachable Service and verify executor ownership and cleanup boundaries.

title: Constrain identities, secrets and network policy
outcome: Separate notebook, Kubernetes, Spark and storage authorization and test a narrow policy.

title: Transfer to cloud storage and scheduling
outcome: Plan an explicitly authorized provider deployment while preserving untested-environment boundaries.

title: Build an incident and acceptance dossier
outcome: Combine source, topology, numerical, recovery and retained-state evidence without promoting planned checks to success.
